messages:

Subject: Request: MAP & security evidence cadence for potential Redwood deployment

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the intro last week — procurement + security are starting to map out the evaluation and we need a concrete mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out the security gates, evidence windows, and DPA redline expectations. To move to procurement review we need: 

- SOC 2 report snapshot (scope & date) and confirmation of any change controls since last assessment
- SIG/CAIQ submission or a sampling approach for CAIQ questions (we typically ask for a 10% sample of high-risk controls, but can accept a full CAIQ spreadsheet)
- Draft DPA (we can share our redlines) and confirmation of data retention & deletion model (retention windows, backups, logs)

Tentative timing: we aim to finish the security & procurement review by Dec 15 to make our Q1 pilot procurement window. Can you send a MAP with owners, milestones, and the evidence checklist? Also flag any required legal exceptions (EU residency, escrow, or on-prem options).

If it helps, I'll loop in Michael Chen (security) after you send the MAP. Attachments: RFP_attachment_list.pdf (see index).

Thanks,
Lisa

Subject: RE: Request: MAP & security evidence cadence for potential Redwood deployment

Lisa — thanks, happy to run this. High-level MAP attached and summary below. I've added Kimberly (security integrations) for the technical intake and Jonas (legal) for DPA negotiation.

Summary (proposed MAP & acceptance lanes)
1) Intake & scope confirm (Nov 26) — owners: ClearVault (Lisa, Michael) + Redwood (Dylan). Deliverable: MAP_Draft_CV-Redwood.xlsx (attached).
2) Evidence sprint (Nov 29 - Dec 6) — owners: Kimberly (Redwood sec eng) + ClearVault security delegates. Deliverables: SOC 2 snapshot, SIG/CAIQ spreadsheet or agreed sample, API endpoint inventory, data flow diagram.
3) Legal redline & DPA review (Dec 3 - Dec 10) — owner: Jonas (Redwood legal) + ClearVault legal. Goal: agree DPA carveouts (EU residency option, limited subprocessor list, retention windows).
4) Final acceptance & signoff (by Dec 15) — acceptance criteria: SOC 2 in-scope items satisfied, SIG high-risk controls verified (sampling results within agreed tolerance), DPA executed or mutually-agreed interim terms in place.

Sampling protocol suggestion for SIG/CAIQ
- For first pass, propose a 10% statistical sample focused on controls tagged as "high" impact in your CAIQ. Redwood will support by providing evidence stubs for controls under our control (infrastructure, key management, access controls).
- If the sample identifies gaps, expand to a targeted secondary sample (additional 10-20% on flagged control families).

Retention & DPA summary (Redwood default positions)
- Application data retention: default 90 days for session-level logs, 365 days for billing metadata; retention beyond 365 days requires explicit carveout and justification.
- Backups: encrypted backups retained for 30 days (separate archival escrow can be negotiated).
- EU residency: available as a Private deployment or hosted EU region for enterprise customers (adds ~2-3 week onboarding timeline).

Attachments: MAP_Draft_CV-Redwood.xlsx (draft milestones and owner matrix), evidence_checklist.txt (technical checklist).

Next steps: please confirm owners for the evidence sprint and whether you prefer a full CAIQ or sample approach.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the clear MAP. We're ok with the MAP timeline but need to align on a couple of points before committing owners: 

1) Attachments: I'm sending SOC2_snapshot_Q3.pdf, SIG_Scan_2026.xlsx (full CAIQ export), and DPA_redlines.docx. Can you confirm Redwood's SOC 2 scope (in-scope services and data planes)? Also flag which CAIQ families you expect to own evidence for vs. which we should test on our side.

2) Sampling: we prefer you run the 10% high-risk sample first. If Redwood provides the CAIQ ownership map (controls we own vs. you own) by EOD Nov 30, we'll assign our security engineer to the sprint.

3) DPA: our redlines include a request for a 180-day retention maximum for audit logs (we'd like logs available for 180 days), and a clause for EU residency for a subset of customer data. If Redwood can't commit to 180 days for logs on hosted, we'll need to evaluate Private deployment or escrow.
